name: Quatre Sept
description: Quatre Sept is a French-Canadian four-player partnership point-trick game with no trumps, descended from Italian Tressette. Players use a 32-card pack (10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7). Holding all four sevens wins the game immediately; winning three consecutive tricks with 10-9-A of a suit (La Politaine) scores an 11-point bonus.

content.text: Quatre Sept is a French-Canadian four-player partnership point-trick game with no trumps, descended from Italian Tressette. Players use a 32-card pack (10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7). Holding all four sevens wins the game immediately; winning three consecutive tricks with 10-9-A of a suit (La Politaine) scores an 11-point bonus.

Quatre Sept is played in the French-speaking provinces of Canada. It descends from the Italian game Tressette, which was fashionable throughout Europe in the 18th century. French players adapted Tressette to the 32-card pack (no 3 or 2), substituting 10 and 9 for those ranks. The game was exported to Canada with the ranking 10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7.
4 players in fixed partnerships. Partners sit opposite each other.
32-card French pack: 10, 9, A, K, Q, J, 8, 7 in each suit. No trumps.
1. Deal 8 cards each in batches of 3-2-3. 2. Deal and play clockwise. 3. If any player has all four sevens, that team wins the game immediately.

items.text: Capot: A team that wins all 8 tricks wins the whole game immediately.
Four 8s: Player dealt all four 8s declares before the first lead; that team wins the game. Replaces or supplements four 7s rule.
Target 32: Game ends at 32 points. If both reach 32 in the same deal, first to claim wins.
Long Game: Play to 200 points for a longer session.
Signals: Tap table = good cards in led suit; slide card = good in same-color suit. Used to signal partner.
Redeal: Hand with no 10s, 9s, or Aces may demand a redeal before first lead.
Pollack: German variant; declarations (Pollack 10-9-A, four of a kind, triplets) score before play; game to 21. No four-7s win.
